findings.excerpt:
refine Finset.sum_bij (fun f _ => cubeFlip f) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro f _
    exact Finset.mem_univ _
  · intro f _ g _ h
    have h' := congrArg cubeFlip h
    simpa only [cubeFlip_cubeFlip] using h'
  · intro g _
    exact ⟨cubeFlip g, Finset.mem_univ _, cubeFlip_cubeFlip g⟩
  · intro f _
    rfl
findings.problem: The proof manually establishes bijectivity and universal-set membership although the preceding involution theorem already supplies the mathematical reason that reindexing preserves the sum.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the proof with:
by
  have hflip : Function.Involutive (cubeFlip : Cube I → Cube I) :=
    cubeFlip_cubeFlip
  exact hflip.bijective.sum_comp F
findings.benefit: Makes the argument explicitly 'an involution is bijective, so reindex the sum', without bookkeeping. It also works when I is empty; no fixed-point-free assumption is introduced.

    !(table (canonicalInput i₀ f) ^^ f i₀)
  cases table (canonicalInput i₀ f) <;> cases f i₀ <;> rfl

  rw [canonicalInput_flip]

theorem canonicalInput_flip (i₀ : I) (f : Cube I) :
    canonicalInput i₀ (cubeFlip f) = canonicalInput i₀ f := by
def cubeFlip (f : Cube I) : Cube I := fun i => !(f i)

induction source with
  | nil => simp [cloneList]
  | cons e es ih =>
      simp only [cloneList, List.flatMap_cons, List.length_append, List.length_map] at *
      rw [ih]
      simp [Nat.add_mul, Nat.add_comm]
findings.problem: The induction reproves the standard length-of-flatMap calculation even though every mapped clone block has the same length.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the proof with:
by
  simp only [cloneList, List.length_flatMap, List.length_map,

findings.benefit: Directly expresses the counting argument: sum one constant block length per source occurrence. Empty sources and repeated equations remain handled without additional assumptions.

evidence.excerpt:
def cloneList (source : List (Equation Name)) : List (Equation (Name × Index)) :=
  source.flatMap fun e => distinctTriples.map (clone e)

theorem length_flatMap {l : List α} {f : α → List β} :
    length (l.flatMap f) = sum (map (fun a => (f a).length) l) := by
@[simp, grind =] theorem length_map {as : List α} (f : α → β) : (as.map f).length = as.length := by

theorem map_const' {l : List α} {b : β} : map (fun _ => b) l = replicate l.length b :=
  map_const
theorem sum_replicate_nat {n : Nat} {a : Nat} : (replicate n a).sum = n * a := by

findings.excerpt:
unfold satisfied
  rw [← h]
  cases assignment e.first <;> cases assignment e.second <;> cases e.rhs <;> rfl
findings.problem: The eight-case truth-table proof hides the simple reason the repeated right-hand variable disappears: XORing a Boolean with itself gives false.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the proof with:
by
  simp only [satisfied, ← h, Bool.xor_assoc, Bool.xor_self, Bool.xor_false]
findings.benefit: Shows reassociation and cancellation directly. It requires no distinctness assumptions, so it still covers equations whose first variable also equals a repeated right-hand variable.

evidence.excerpt:
def satisfied (e : Equation Name) (g : Name → Bool) : Bool :=
  (xor (xor (g e.first) (g e.second)) (g e.third)) == e.rhs
theorem xor_assoc : ∀ (x y z : Bool), ((x ^^ y) ^^ z) = (x ^^ (y ^^ z)) := bne_assoc
theorem xor_self : ∀ (x : Bool), (x ^^ x) = false := by decide
theorem xor_false : ∀ (x : Bool), (x ^^ false) = x := bne_false
